advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Change the default AUTOLANDER_PORT (and the fetch-secrets.sh / Dockerfile ENV / autodeploy defaults) off 8080 so the autolander host publish does not collide with Gerrit's 127.0.0.1:8080.
evidence: infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:38: `- "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"` (gerrit)
infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:130: `- "127.0.0.1:${AUTOLANDER_PORT:-8080}:8080"` (autolander)
infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh diff: `echo "AUTOLANDER_PORT=8080"` — the operative default really is 8080
infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:17: `# container ports: Gerrit on 127.0.0.1:8080, review-bot on 127.0.0.1:${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}.`
advisory.finding: Host-port collision: the autolander service publishes 127.0.0.1:${AUTOLANDER_PORT:-8080}:8080 and fetch-secrets.sh writes AUTOLANDER_PORT=8080, but Gerrit already publishes 127.0.0.1:8080:8080. Two services binding the same host loopback socket cannot both start — `docker compose up` will fail with an address-in-use bind error for whichever container starts second.
scenarios: compose-up.sh brings up gerrit + autolander on the same host
advisory.suggested_fix: Pick a distinct host port for the autolander status endpoint (e.g. AUTOLANDER_PORT=8081) in fetch-secrets.sh, Dockerfile.autolander ENV, and the autodeploy AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL default; keep the container-internal port at 8080.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure AUTOLANDER_PORT resolves to the autolander's own distinct host port so /autolander/status does not proxy to Gerrit.
evidence: diff: `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:${AUTOLANDER_PORT}/;`
infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:86: gerrit `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;`
infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh diff: `echo "AUTOLANDER_PORT=8080"`
advisory.finding: nginx /autolander/status proxies to 127.0.0.1:${AUTOLANDER_PORT}, which with the default port 8080 is Gerrit's published port — so GET /autolander/status reaches Gerrit, not the auto-lander status endpoint.
scenarios: Operator/monitoring hits https://.../autolander/status expecting the loop's JSON status

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Point AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL at the auto-lander's own distinct host port (not 8080), so the deploy health check cannot pass by hitting Gerrit.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:51: `AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL="${AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL:-http://localhost:8080/}"  # auto-lander status endpoint (NOT Gerrit)`
infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:38: gerrit publishes `127.0.0.1:8080:8080`
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:186 (review-bot pattern) uses `curl -fsS -m 3 "$HEALTH_URL"` — same probe shape reused for autolander
advisory.finding: autodeploy AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL defaults to http://localhost:8080/, which is Gerrit's published host port — the post-deploy health check will succeed against Gerrit and report the auto-lander healthy even when the loop is down, defeating the rollback-on-unhealthy contract. The inline comment even claims '(NOT Gerrit)'.
scenarios: An autolander deploy where the loop fails to start but Gerrit is up

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Use GET /changes/{id}?o=CURRENT_REVISION&o=DETAILED_ACCOUNTS (the query endpoint that returns the revisions map) to read revisions[current].uploader in the smoke check, so step 5 actually asserts uploader preservation.
evidence: smoke-check-autolander.sh:109: `"${GERRIT_BASE_URL}/a/changes/${SMOKE_CHANGE}/detail?o=CURRENT_REVISION&o=DETAILED_ACCOUNTS"`
smoke-check-autolander.sh:115-117: parses `d.get("current_revision")` then `revisions[cur].uploader` — fields the /detail endpoint does not populate
smoke-check-autolander.sh:121-122: empty uploader takes the non-fatal WARN branch
advisory.finding: The smoke-check reads the rebased patch set uploader from GET /changes/{id}/detail, but the `revisions` map (and thus revisions[current].uploader) is returned by the change query endpoint (GET /changes/{id}?o=CURRENT_REVISION), not by /detail. The parse will almost always yield an empty username and silently take the WARN branch, so the uploader-preservation assertion (step 5) never actually runs.
scenarios: A full smoke run with a staged SMOKE_CHANGE reaching step 5
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the `/detail?...` URL with `/a/changes/${SMOKE_CHANGE}/?o=CURRENT_REVISION&o=DETAILED_ACCOUNTS` (the change-query endpoint populates `revisions`).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the smoke-check header (step 4) with the actual POST body — either send the documented `base` or drop it from the doc.
evidence: smoke-check-autolander.sh header step 4: `POST /a/changes/{id}/rebase with {"base":"<new tip>","on_behalf_of_uploader":true}`
smoke-check-autolander.sh:87: `-d '{"on_behalf_of_uploader": true}'`
advisory.finding: The smoke-check's documented rebase call (step 4 in the header) posts {"base":"<new tip>","on_behalf_of_uploader":true}, but the actual curl omits the `base` field and posts only {"on_behalf_of_uploader": true}. The docstring and implementation disagree; without an explicit base the rebase targets the branch tip, which changes what the check exercises versus what it documents.
scenarios: Operator reads the header to understand what the canary validates

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the per-ref rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader access-right (vs the ticket's All-Projects capability) is the intended, agreed mechanism and update the S5b ticket/file_impact to match.
evidence: ticket 3c55 AC S5b: "the `All-Projects` `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` capability + submit ACL via `setup-all-projects.sh`"
ticket file_impact: infra/gerrit/setup-project.sh "All-Projects [capability] rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader"
project.config diff: grants added under `[access "refs/heads/*"]` as `rebase`/`rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader = group Contributors`
commit message: "the per-ref Gerrit `rebase` + `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` access rights ... (NOT a global capability ...)"
advisory.finding: Scope/approach drift from the ticket: the S5b AC and file_impact call for the grant as an All-Projects `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` CAPABILITY (via setup-all-projects.sh), but the diff instead adds it (plus `rebase`) as a per-ref ACCESS RIGHT on refs/heads/* in the rebar project.config. The per-ref form is a valid Gerrit mechanism, but it diverges from the stated plan and from the referenced provisioning script (setup-all-projects.sh is not touched).
scenarios: Reconciling the delivered ACL against the epic/story plan and the file_impact contract

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the 127.0.0.1:8080 host-port collision between the Gerrit service and the autolander service (Gerrit already publishes 8080).
evidence: docker-compose.yml:38: `- "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"` (gerrit)
docker-compose.yml:130: `- "127.0.0.1:${AUTOLANDER_PORT:-8080}:8080"` (autolander)
infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh:114: `echo "AUTOLANDER_PORT=8080"` — the generated .env pins the host port to 8080, the same loopback port Gerrit binds
advisory.finding: Host-port collision on 127.0.0.1:8080: the Gerrit service already publishes `127.0.0.1:8080:8080`, and the new autolander service publishes `127.0.0.1:${AUTOLANDER_PORT:-8080}:8080` with fetch-secrets.sh hard-writing AUTOLANDER_PORT=8080 — so `docker compose up` will fail with a port-already-allocated bind conflict on the loopback:8080 endpoint.
scenarios: A clean `compose-up.sh` / `docker compose up -d` on the host after this change
autodeploy rebuild of the autolander service
advisory.suggested_fix: Choose a distinct default host port for the autolander (e.g. AUTOLANDER_PORT=8090) in fetch-secrets.sh and the compose/Dockerfile/nginx/autodeploy references; keep the container port 8080 but map to a free host port.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Point AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL at the autolander's actual published host port, not Gerrit's 8080.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:51: `AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL="${AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL:-http://localhost:8080/}"  # auto-lander status endpoint (NOT Gerrit)`
docker-compose.yml:38: gerrit publishes `127.0.0.1:8080:8080` — localhost:8080 is Gerrit
autodeploy.sh:186-190: the health loop curls $AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL and rolls back to :prev on failure
advisory.finding: The autodeploy autolander health-check URL `http://localhost:8080/` points at Gerrit's published host port (127.0.0.1:8080), not the autolander — so the post-deploy health probe and rollback decision would be driven by Gerrit's response, defeating the intended autolander liveness gate.
scenarios: autodeploy runs on a main advance that touches AUTOLANDER_PATHS
advisory.suggested_fix: After picking a non-conflicting AUTOLANDER_PORT, set the default to `http://localhost:${AUTOLANDER_PORT}/` so the probe hits the autolander, not Gerrit.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the willfarrell/autoheal image to a specific tag or (preferably) a sha256 digest.
evidence: docker-compose.yml:149: `image: willfarrell/autoheal` — no `:tag`/`@sha256` digest
docker-compose.yml:155-156: `- /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock` (RW socket)
Gerrit is pinned (`gerritcodereview/gerrit:3.14.1`, compose-up.sh:18) and the bot images are locally built — this sidecar is the only unpinned image
advisory.finding: The autoheal sidecar image `willfarrell/autoheal` is declared with no tag or digest pin, so it resolves to `:latest` — a non-idempotent, drift-prone, unvetted-upstream dependency, notable because this container is mounted the Docker socket read-write and can restart containers.
scenarios: A rebuild/pull pulls a new upstream :latest with changed behavior
supply-chain: a compromised upstream tag lands on a container with RW Docker socket

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader grant against ADR-0042 item 7 (confirm whether the separate per-ref grant is actually required) and fix whichever is wrong.
evidence: infra/gerrit/project.config:76-77: `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader = group Contributors` / `= group Administrators`
docs/adr/0042-auto-lander.md:172-173: 'the on-behalf half needs no extra grant (it checks the original uploader’s existing push right)'
project.config:67-68 comment asserts the REST option 'requires the caller to hold BOTH the `rebase` permission AND the per-ref `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` permission' — direct contradiction of the ADR
advisory.finding: The added per-ref `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` grant may be broader than required: ADR-0042 (item 7) states the on-behalf half 'needs no extra grant (it checks the original uploader's existing push right)', contradicting the project.config change which grants `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` to Contributors+Administrators. This should be reconciled to avoid granting an ACL that is unnecessary (least-privilege).
scenarios: Applying refs/meta/config with a grant the ADR says is unnecessary

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Redirect AUTOLANDER_OFFSET_FILE in test_observability_exit.py's healthy_env and add an assertion covering the §4e marker-delta / unhealthy-state output.
evidence: observability.sh:191 `AUTOLANDER_OFFSET_FILE="${AUTOLANDER_OFFSET_FILE:-/var/lib/rebar/autolander-fail-offset}"` with `mkdir -p "$(dirname ...)"` at :192 and `echo "$altotal" >"$AUTOLANDER_OFFSET_FILE"` at :202
test_observability_exit.py:71-80 env.update sets REPL_OFFSET_FILE/VOTER_OFFSET_FILE/MERGE_OFFSET_FILE/DEPLOY_OFFSET_FILE/G2P_OFFSET_FILE but NOT AUTOLANDER_OFFSET_FILE

ABSENCE: no assertion in tests/scripts/ exercises the §4e marker-delta / clamp / unhealthy-state summation (`alnew`/`alsum`); the only assertion is `result.returncode == 0` (test_observability_exit.py:92)
advisory.finding: The observability.sh §4e test isolation was not extended for the new AUTOLANDER_OFFSET_FILE: test_observability_exit.py redirects every other feeder's offset file away from /var/lib/rebar but not this one, so the healthy-run test writes to the real host path /var/lib/rebar/autolander-fail-offset (isolation leak), and no test asserts the new §4e arithmetic (offset delta, negative-delta clamp, docker unhealthy summation).
scenarios: Running the observability test suite on a dev/CI box writes/overwrites the real /var/lib/rebar/autolander-fail-offset
A regression in the §4e delta or negative-clamp logic (e.g. the grep -c exit-code sharp edge the comment warns about) would not be caught
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `"AUTOLANDER_OFFSET_FILE": str(off / "autolander")` to the env.update block, and add a case to the journalctl/docker stubs plus an assertion on the published autolander_errors value (e.g. via the aws stub capturing --value).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make smoke-check-autolander.sh fail (not WARN) when the rebased patch set uploader cannot be read, so the uploader-preservation assertion cannot be silently skipped.
evidence: smoke-check-autolander.sh:119 `' 2>/dev/null || true)"` — any python/parse failure yields an empty uploader_username
smoke-check-autolander.sh:121-122 `if [ -z "${uploader_username}" ]; then echo "...WARN — could not read... skipping the uploader-preservation assertion..."` (non-fatal)
smoke-check-autolander.sh:129 final `echo "smoke-check-autolander: PASS — ...grant verified."` still runs after the WARN branch
advisory.finding: smoke-check-autolander.sh's step-5 uploader-preservation assertion — the only check that on_behalf_of_uploader actually took effect (preserving the original uploader vs the bot) — is downgraded to a non-fatal WARN when the uploader cannot be parsed, and the parse swallows all errors (`2>/dev/null || true`), so the canary prints PASS with the assertion never executing.
scenarios: Gerrit detail response shape changes, XSSI stripping misfires, or python3 is unavailable → empty parse → WARN → PASS
rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader grant silently not taking effect but the HTTP 200 (step 4) passing
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the `[ -z "${uploader_username}" ]` branch from an echo/WARN to `fail "could not read the rebased patch set uploader — cannot verify on_behalf_of_uploader took effect"`, and drop the `|| true` so a python parse failure is surfaced.
